metadata.disclaimer: Based on publicly available NIST AI RMF Playbook and SP 800-53 Rev 5 cross-references. Governance and policy subcategories map well; AI-specific technical subcategories have limited SP 800-53 coverage. Validate with qualified assessors for compliance/audit use.

clauses.title: Legal and Regulatory Alignment
clauses.rationale: PL-01, PM-01, CA-01, and SA-01 provide policy and planning controls that cover organisational compliance obligations for information security. PT-01 and SR-01 extend this to privacy and supply chain, partially addressing the broad legal alignment required by AI RMF.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.1.1 requires alignment with AI-specific legal and regulatory requirements including algorithmic accountability laws, AI liability frameworks, and sector-specific AI regulations. SP 800-53 policies address security and privacy compliance but do not cover AI-specific legal obligations such as EU AI Act requirements, algorithmic transparency laws, or AI liability provisions.

clauses.title: Trustworthy AI Characteristics
clauses.rationale: PM-01 and PM-02 establish organisational risk management programmes. PL-01 and RA-01 provide policy and risk assessment foundations. PM-09 risk management strategy partially covers the structured approach needed for trustworthy AI characteristics.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.1.2 requires policies explicitly addressing AI trustworthiness characteristics: validity, reliability, safety, security, explainability, fairness, bias management, privacy, and accountability. SP 800-53 covers security and privacy but not AI-specific trustworthiness dimensions such as algorithmic fairness, AI explainability, or responsible AI principles.

clauses.title: Organizational Risk Tolerance for AI
clauses.rationale: RA-03 risk assessment and PM-09 risk management strategy provide the foundation for articulating risk tolerance. RA-07 risk response and PM-28 criticality analysis support structured risk appetite decisions. PL-10 baseline selection reflects risk tolerance in control selection.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.1.3 requires organisation-wide AI risk tolerance thresholds covering AI-specific risk categories such as bias tolerance, model uncertainty thresholds, and acceptable false positive/negative rates. SP 800-53 risk tolerance focuses on information security risk and does not address AI-specific risk appetite dimensions.

clauses.title: Organisational Teams and Responsibilities
clauses.rationale: PL-02 system security plans and PM-01 programme policies define organisational roles. SA-05 documentation requirements and CM-01 configuration management policy support process documentation for teams involved in AI system lifecycle.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.1.4 requires cross-functional AI governance teams including AI ethics boards, AI review committees, and multi-disciplinary oversight groups. SP 800-53 organisational structure controls address security roles but do not require AI-specific governance bodies, ethics committees, or interdisciplinary AI oversight structures.

clauses.title: Organisational Risk Policies and Monitoring
clauses.rationale: CA-07 continuous monitoring and SI-04 system monitoring provide operational risk monitoring. IR-01 and IR-08 incident response planning with AU-06 audit review form a monitoring and response cycle aligned with organisational risk policy execution.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.1.5 requires monitoring policies specific to AI risk indicators including model performance degradation, bias drift, and AI system behaviour anomalies. SP 800-53 monitoring controls focus on security events and vulnerabilities, not AI-specific risk signals such as model drift or fairness metric changes.

clauses.title: Policies for AI Risks from Third Parties
clauses.rationale: PM-05 information system inventory and CM-08 component inventory help track third-party AI components. PM-01 programme policies and SA-05 documentation requirements support policy articulation for third-party AI risk management.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.1.6 requires explicit policies addressing AI-specific third-party risks including pre-trained model bias, training data provenance from vendors, and third-party AI system transparency. SP 800-53 third-party policies address supply chain security but not AI-specific third-party risk dimensions such as model bias inheritance or vendor responsible AI practices.

clauses.title: Processes for AI Decommissioning
clauses.rationale: CM-12 information location and MP-06 media sanitisation cover data disposal aspects of decommissioning. SA-12 supply chain protection and SA-04 acquisition requirements include lifecycle considerations. SR-12 component disposal addresses hardware end-of-life.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.1.7 requires AI-specific decommissioning processes covering model retirement procedures, training data disposal, model artefact deletion, and documentation of decommissioning decisions. SP 800-53 decommissioning controls focus on system and media disposal but not AI-specific artefacts such as model weights, training datasets, or AI decision logs.

clauses.title: Roles and Responsibilities for AI Risk
clauses.rationale: PM-02 senior information security officer and PS-01 personnel security policy establish accountability structures. AC-05 separation of duties and PM-29 risk management oversight formalise role boundaries. PS-09 position descriptions documents role-specific security responsibilities.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.2.1 requires AI-specific role definitions including AI risk owner, AI ethics officer, AI product manager, and AI developer roles with distinct accountability for AI trustworthiness. SP 800-53 role accountability focuses on security and privacy roles and does not address AI governance roles or AI ethics accountability structures.

clauses.title: AI Risk Awareness and Training
clauses.rationale: AT-01 through AT-03 awareness and training policy, awareness, and training programmes provide a strong foundation. AT-06 training feedback allows evaluation of training effectiveness. PM-13 information security workforce development supports broader skill-building applicable to AI risk competencies.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.2.2 requires AI-specific training covering responsible AI principles, AI bias awareness, AI ethics, and AI risk management techniques. SP 800-53 training controls address security and privacy awareness but do not include AI-specific literacy, fairness concepts, or responsible AI development practices.

clauses.title: Executive Accountability for AI
clauses.rationale: PM-02 senior information security officer and PM-29 risk management oversight establish senior-level accountability. PM-01 programme policies and PL-09 central management of plans provide governance structures applicable to executive AI accountability.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.2.3 requires explicit board and executive accountability for AI risk decisions including approval of AI deployment decisions, AI ethics commitments, and AI risk acceptance. SP 800-53 executive accountability focuses on information security and does not require AI-specific board oversight, AI ethics leadership, or executive AI risk governance.

clauses.title: Diverse AI Teams
clauses.rationale: PM-02 and PS-01 cover workforce management and personnel policy. PM-13 information security workforce development partially supports building diverse teams. Coverage is limited as SP 800-53 does not address diversity requirements.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. AI RMF GOVERN.3.1 requires diversity, equity, and inclusion considerations in AI teams to reduce bias and blind spots. This includes interdisciplinary composition, demographic diversity, and domain expertise diversity. SP 800-53 does not address workforce diversity, team composition, or inclusive AI development practices.

clauses.title: Policies for Diverse AI Teams
clauses.rationale: AC-01 access control policy and PL-04 rules of behaviour provide behavioural frameworks for personnel. PM-02 programme management and SA-08 security engineering principles cover some organisational policy dimensions applicable to team governance.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.3.2 requires organisational policies explicitly supporting diverse and inclusive AI teams, including mechanisms for surfacing dissenting viewpoints and psychological safety for raising bias concerns. SP 800-53 does not address team diversity policies, inclusive culture requirements, or mechanisms for surfacing AI ethics concerns.

clauses.title: Organisational Culture for AI Risk
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy and RA-03 risk assessment provide structured risk management foundations. PM-02 programme management and CA-02 security assessments support organisational risk culture through formal processes.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.4.1 requires an organisational culture that values AI risk management, responsible AI practices, and psychological safety for raising AI concerns. SP 800-53 focuses on procedural risk management and does not address cultural dimensions, leadership tone on responsible AI, or organisational norms around AI ethics.

clauses.title: Organisational Teams Committed to AI Risk
clauses.rationale: RA-08 privacy impact assessments and PM-28 criticality analysis require designated teams to perform structured assessments. CA-02 security assessments and RA-03 risk assessment establish team-based risk evaluation processes relevant to cross-functional AI risk commitment.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.4.2 requires cross-functional teams with explicit commitment to AI risk management including dedicated AI ethics review processes, red teaming for AI systems, and structured bias review workflows. SP 800-53 assessment and review teams focus on security but not AI-specific review processes or ethical red-teaming.

clauses.title: Feedback Mechanisms for AI Risk
clauses.rationale: CA-02 security assessments and CA-07 continuous monitoring provide structured feedback loops. IR-06 incident reporting and IR-08 incident response plan updates create mechanisms for incorporating lessons learned into ongoing risk management.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.4.3 requires feedback channels for reporting AI bias, unintended consequences, and AI safety concerns from users, operators, and affected communities. SP 800-53 feedback mechanisms focus on security incidents and audit findings, not AI-specific user feedback channels, bias reporting mechanisms, or community impact feedback loops.

clauses.title: Organisational Risk Tolerance Policies
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy formally documents risk tolerance. RA-03 risk assessment, PM-28 criticality analysis, and RA-07 risk response provide structured risk treatment aligned with tolerance thresholds. PL-10 baseline selection operationalises risk tolerance in control selection.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.5.1 requires explicit risk tolerance policies for AI-specific risk categories including acceptable AI error rates, bias thresholds, and model uncertainty limits. SP 800-53 risk tolerance policies address information security risk and do not define AI-specific risk boundaries or acceptable performance degradation thresholds.

clauses.title: Third-Party AI Risk Policies
clauses.rationale: SA-09 external information system services and SR-01 through SR-03 supply chain risk management policy and planning establish third-party risk management frameworks. SR-05 acquisition strategies and tools support structured vendor risk assessment applicable to AI suppliers.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.5.2 requires policies specifically addressing AI supply chain risks including pre-trained model bias, training data provenance from third parties, and AI vendor responsible AI certifications. SP 800-53 supply chain policies address security and integrity but not AI-specific vendor assessment criteria such as model transparency or vendor bias disclosures.

clauses.title: AI Policies for Incident Response
clauses.rationale: IR-04 incident handling and CP-02 contingency plan provide incident response foundations. SA-09 external services and SR-06 supplier assessments address third-party incident coordination, relevant to AI system incidents involving third-party components.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.6.1 requires incident response policies covering AI-specific incidents including bias events, unintended AI behaviour, and AI safety failures. SP 800-53 incident response policies are security-focused and do not address AI-specific incident classification, AI bias incident response, or AI safety event escalation procedures.

clauses.title: Policies for Emerging AI Risks
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy and RA-07 risk response provide mechanisms for incorporating emerging risks. CA-02 security assessments and PL-10 baseline selection allow policy updates as new threats emerge, partially applicable to evolving AI risks.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF GOVERN.6.2 requires policies for monitoring and responding to emerging AI-specific risks including new adversarial techniques, newly discovered bias types, and evolving AI safety vulnerabilities. SP 800-53 emerging risk policies address new security vulnerabilities but not AI-specific emerging risks such as generative AI misuse, novel adversarial attacks on ML models, or emerging AI accountability standards.

clauses.title: AI Use Case Context and Intended Purpose
clauses.rationale: RA-03 risk assessment and PM-11 mission and business process definition require articulating system purpose and context. SA-03 system development lifecycle and PM-28 criticality analysis support structured context documentation applicable to AI use case definition.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.1.1 requires detailed documentation of the intended AI use case including deployment context, intended users, geographic scope, and operational constraints. SP 800-53 context documentation focuses on information security mission impact and does not address AI-specific deployment context such as high-risk application domains or vulnerable population considerations.

clauses.title: Interdisciplinary AI Teams
clauses.rationale: PM-02 programme management and SA-03 system development lifecycle support team organisation. PM-13 information security workforce development partially covers building multi-disciplinary security teams applicable to interdisciplinary AI development contexts.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.1.2 requires interdisciplinary teams for AI context mapping including domain experts, social scientists, ethicists, legal experts, and user representatives. SP 800-53 does not address interdisciplinary team composition, sociotechnical expertise requirements, or domain expert inclusion in AI system development.

clauses.title: AI Risk Classification and Categorisation
clauses.rationale: PL-01 information security policy and PM-09 risk management strategy provide classification frameworks. PM-08 critical infrastructure plan supports risk tiering applicable to high-impact AI deployments in critical sectors.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.1.3 requires AI-specific risk categorisation covering potential harm severity, population affected, reversibility of harm, and AI system autonomy level. SP 800-53 risk categorisation uses FIPS 199 impact levels for security but does not address AI-specific harm categories, societal impact tiers, or vulnerability-weighted risk classification.

clauses.title: Stakeholder Identification for AI
clauses.rationale: RA-03 risk assessment and PM-11 mission and business process definition require identifying stakeholders affected by system risk. PM-28 criticality analysis and RA-07 risk response support structured stakeholder impact assessment relevant to AI system affected parties.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.1.4 requires comprehensive identification of AI-affected stakeholders including end users, operators, directly affected communities, and indirectly impacted populations. SP 800-53 stakeholder identification focuses on mission owners and authorising officials, not AI system beneficiaries, affected communities, or vulnerable populations.

clauses.title: Organisational Risk Tolerance Alignment
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy documents organisational risk tolerance. RA-03 risk assessment and RA-07 risk response operationalise tolerance thresholds. PL-10 baseline selection aligns control implementation with risk tolerance decisions.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.1.5 requires mapping specific AI system risks against organisational AI risk tolerance thresholds, including bias tolerance, reliability thresholds, and acceptable AI error rates. SP 800-53 risk tolerance alignment is security-focused and does not address AI-specific tolerance mapping for fairness, reliability, or safety thresholds.

clauses.title: Practices and Principles for AI
clauses.rationale: SA-03 system development lifecycle and SA-04 acquisition requirements embed security practices. SA-08 security engineering principles provides a structured framework. PL-01 policy and PM-11 mission definition support principled system design applicable to responsible AI practices.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.1.6 requires application of responsible AI practices and principles including human-centred design, fairness by design, and explainability requirements during AI system scoping. SP 800-53 engineering and acquisition principles address security but not AI-specific responsible design principles such as fairness, explainability, or privacy-preserving ML techniques.

clauses.title: Scientific Validity of AI Approaches
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition requirements and SA-08 security engineering principles require technical validity in system design. SA-11 developer security testing provides validation requirements. PL-01 policy supports documentation of technical standards applicable to AI approach validity.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.2.1 requires assessment of the scientific validity and technical soundness of the chosen AI approach including model suitability, training methodology validity, and evaluation methodology rigor. SP 800-53 does not address AI model scientific validity, ML methodology soundness, or the appropriateness of AI approaches for specific problem domains.

clauses.title: AI System Failure Modes
clauses.rationale: SA-08 security engineering principles and SA-04 acquisition requirements address failure mode analysis in design. CP-02 contingency planning considers failure scenarios. SA-11 developer security testing and SA-05 documentation requirements support failure mode documentation.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.2.2 requires identification of AI-specific failure modes including distribution shift failures, adversarial input failures, out-of-distribution failures, and model collapse scenarios. SP 800-53 failure mode analysis focuses on security failures and availability, not AI-specific failure patterns such as concept drift, model degradation, or adversarial vulnerabilities.

clauses.title: Scientific Principles for AI Trustworthiness
clauses.rationale: CA-02 security assessments and SA-11 developer security testing provide rigorous evaluation frameworks. RA-05 vulnerability scanning and CA-07 continuous monitoring support ongoing trustworthiness assessment. CA-05 plan of action and milestones drives remediation of identified gaps.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.2.3 requires application of scientific evaluation principles to AI trustworthiness including standardised bias benchmarks, robustness evaluation protocols, and interpretability assessments. SP 800-53 assessment frameworks address security but do not include AI-specific evaluation standards for fairness metrics, robustness benchmarks, or explainability measures.

clauses.title: Benefits of AI Deployment
clauses.rationale: PM-28 criticality analysis requires assessment of system importance and value. RA-08 privacy impact assessments capture some benefit-risk trade-offs. SA-03 system development lifecycle includes purpose documentation partially applicable to AI benefit analysis.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.3.1 requires structured analysis of intended benefits including accuracy improvements, efficiency gains, and access improvements, weighed against potential harms. SP 800-53 does not address AI benefit-harm analysis, intended positive outcomes documentation, or structured AI value proposition assessment.

clauses.title: Scientific Validity of AI Impact Assessment
clauses.rationale: RA-03 risk assessment and RA-08 privacy impact assessments provide structured impact evaluation. PM-28 criticality analysis and RA-07 risk response support evidence-based impact decision-making applicable to AI impact assessment processes.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.3.2 requires scientifically grounded AI impact assessment including quantitative bias measurement, statistical fairness evaluation, and validated impact metrics. SP 800-53 impact assessments address security and privacy impacts but not AI-specific impact measurement methodologies, algorithmic fairness metrics, or societal harm quantification.

clauses.title: AI Deployment Context Documentation
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition requirements and SA-08 engineering principles support deployment context documentation. PM-09 risk management strategy contextualises deployment risk. SA-11 developer testing requirements document deployment validation activities.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.3.3 requires documentation of AI deployment context including operational environment constraints, user population characteristics, and contextual factors affecting AI performance. SP 800-53 deployment documentation focuses on security configuration and does not address AI operational context, user population demographics, or deployment environment AI-specific risk factors.

clauses.title: Risks of AI to Affected Groups
clauses.rationale: SA-05 documentation requirements and SA-04 acquisition requirements provide risk documentation frameworks. AT-04 training records and PL-04 rules of behaviour support awareness of risks to affected groups, partially applicable to AI harm documentation.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.3.4 requires identification of differential risks to specific affected groups including potential discrimination, disproportionate negative impacts on marginalised populations, and intersectional harm analysis. SP 800-53 does not address group-specific harm assessment, protected characteristic risk analysis, or equity impact evaluation.

clauses.title: Likelihood of AI Risks
clauses.rationale: PM-02 programme management and CA-07 continuous monitoring support structured risk likelihood assessment. AC-01 access control policy and PL-04 rules of behaviour provide behavioural governance applicable to human-caused AI risk scenarios.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.3.5 requires probabilistic likelihood assessment for AI-specific risks including probability of model failure, likelihood of bias manifestation, and frequency of harmful outputs. SP 800-53 likelihood assessment focuses on threat likelihood for security risks and does not address AI-specific probability estimation for bias events, model failures, or AI safety incidents.

clauses.title: Third-Party AI Risk Evaluation
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition requirements and SA-09 external services establish third-party risk evaluation frameworks. SR-05 acquisition strategies and SR-06 supplier assessments provide structured vendor evaluation. SA-05 documentation requirements support third-party risk documentation.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.4.1 requires evaluation of third-party AI systems for AI-specific risks including pre-trained model bias, training data quality, and responsible AI practices of AI vendors. SP 800-53 third-party evaluation covers security and supply chain risks but not AI-specific vendor criteria such as model transparency, bias disclosures, or AI ethics certifications.

clauses.title: Third-Party AI Components Inventory
clauses.rationale: SR-03 supply chain controls and SR-01 supply chain policy establish inventory and control frameworks for third-party components. RA-05 vulnerability scanning and SA-09 external services support ongoing third-party risk monitoring applicable to third-party AI component tracking.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.4.2 requires comprehensive inventory of third-party AI components including pre-trained models, AI APIs, AI datasets, and AI development tools with provenance and bias risk documentation. SP 800-53 inventory controls cover software components and supply chain but not AI-specific component attributes such as model provenance, training data sourcing, or bias evaluation records.

clauses.title: Likelihood and Impact of AI Risks
clauses.rationale: RA-03 risk assessment formally combines likelihood and impact assessments. RA-07 risk response and PM-09 risk management strategy support structured risk prioritisation. CA-02 security assessments validate risk assessments against organisational risk tolerance.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MAP.5.1 requires combined likelihood and impact assessment for AI-specific risks using AI-appropriate risk methodologies that account for model uncertainty, distributional shift, and evolving deployment contexts. SP 800-53 risk combination methods address security risk but do not accommodate AI-specific risk dimensions such as model uncertainty quantification or temporal risk evolution.

clauses.title: AI Risk Treatment Decisions
clauses.rationale: PM-03 information security resources and PM-09 risk management strategy support resource allocation for risk treatment. PM-02 programme management and RA-03 risk assessment provide the decision framework for selecting and authorising risk treatment options.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.1.1 requires structured AI risk treatment decision processes including accept, transfer, mitigate, and avoid decisions with AI-specific criteria. SP 800-53 risk treatment focuses on security risk treatment options and does not address AI-specific treatment decisions such as model decommissioning, bias mitigation selection, or human-in-the-loop intervention thresholds.

clauses.title: AI Risk Prioritisation
clauses.rationale: IR-04 incident handling and IR-08 incident response plan provide structured risk prioritisation for active threats. RA-07 risk response and PM-09 risk management strategy establish prioritisation frameworks. CA-05 plan of action and milestones operationalises prioritised remediation.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.1.2 requires AI risk prioritisation frameworks accounting for AI-specific factors such as speed of harm propagation, scale of affected population, and reversibility of AI-caused harm. SP 800-53 prioritisation frameworks focus on security risk severity and do not address AI-specific prioritisation criteria such as bias impact breadth or model failure cascade effects.

clauses.title: AI Risk Response and Residual Risk
clauses.rationale: RA-07 risk response provides a structured framework for selecting and implementing risk treatments. CA-07 continuous monitoring tracks residual risk after treatment. PM-09 risk management strategy and RA-03 risk assessment support residual risk documentation and acceptance decisions.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.1.3 requires documentation and acceptance of residual AI risks including residual bias risks, model uncertainty acceptance, and documentation of limitations accepted for deployment. SP 800-53 residual risk acceptance covers security risks but does not address AI-specific residual risks such as accepted bias thresholds, known model limitations, or AI safety caveats.

clauses.title: Negative AI Risk Interventions
clauses.rationale: RA-07 risk response and PM-09 risk management strategy support intervention selection and planning. PM-04 plan of action and milestones management and CA-02 security assessments provide structured review of intervention effectiveness.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.1.4 requires evaluation of whether AI risk interventions themselves introduce new negative consequences, including over-correction bias, false safety assurance, and performance trade-offs from bias mitigation. SP 800-53 does not address second-order effects of AI risk treatments or the risk of mitigation measures introducing new AI failure modes.

clauses.title: AI Risk Treatment Implementation
clauses.rationale: CA-05 plan of action and milestones drives structured implementation of risk treatments. SI-04 monitoring verifies treatment effectiveness. RA-07 risk response and RA-03 risk assessment support treatment selection. SA-11 developer security testing validates treatment implementation.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.2.1 requires implementation of AI-specific risk treatments including bias mitigation techniques, model constraint implementation, and fairness-aware training procedures. SP 800-53 treatment implementation focuses on security controls and does not address AI-specific mitigation techniques such as algorithmic debiasing, fairness constraints, or differential privacy implementation.

clauses.title: AI System Monitoring and Evaluation
clauses.rationale: CA-07 continuous monitoring and SI-04 system monitoring provide strong operational monitoring foundations. AU-06 audit review and AU-12 audit record generation support structured evaluation and reporting of monitoring findings applicable to AI system performance tracking.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.2.2 requires AI-specific monitoring including model performance metrics, fairness metric tracking, data drift detection, and concept drift monitoring. SP 800-53 monitoring focuses on security events and vulnerabilities; AI-specific monitoring for model accuracy degradation, bias drift, or feature distribution shifts requires supplementation.

clauses.title: AI Incident Response
clauses.rationale: IR-04 incident handling and IR-08 incident response plan provide structured incident management. CP-02 contingency planning supports continuity during AI incidents. CM-03 configuration change control supports rollback and remediation applicable to AI model incidents.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.2.3 requires AI-specific incident response procedures including bias incident response, model rollback procedures, AI safety event escalation, and stakeholder notification for AI incidents. SP 800-53 incident response covers security incidents but does not address AI-specific incident types, model rollback procedures, or bias event containment and communication.

clauses.title: AI Risk Treatments for Third Parties
clauses.rationale: SA-09 external services and SR-06 supplier assessments provide third-party risk treatment frameworks. SR-03 supply chain controls and SA-04 acquisition requirements embed treatment requirements in vendor relationships. CA-07 monitoring extends oversight to third-party AI components.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.2.4 requires AI-specific third-party risk treatments including contractual AI responsible use requirements, third-party model bias testing requirements, and AI vendor audit rights. SP 800-53 third-party treatments address security requirements but not AI-specific vendor obligations for bias testing, model transparency, or responsible AI commitments.

clauses.title: Pre-Trained Model Risk Assessment
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition requirements and SA-09 external services require risk assessment for acquired components. SR-03 supply chain controls and CM-08 component inventory support tracking of pre-trained models as third-party components in the AI system inventory.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.3.1 requires assessment of pre-trained models for AI-specific risks including inherited biases, training data issues, known failure modes, and alignment with the intended deployment context. SP 800-53 acquisition and supply chain controls do not address pre-trained model bias evaluation, training data provenance assessment, or model capability verification for specific use cases.

clauses.title: Pre-Trained Model Monitoring
clauses.rationale: CA-07 continuous monitoring and RA-05 vulnerability scanning provide ongoing monitoring of third-party components. SA-11 developer security testing validates model behaviour. AU-06 audit review supports systematic review of monitoring findings for pre-trained model performance.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.3.2 requires ongoing monitoring of pre-trained models for performance drift, emerging bias patterns, and vendor model updates that may affect deployed system behaviour. SP 800-53 monitoring covers security vulnerabilities and system integrity but not AI-specific pre-trained model monitoring such as model version change impact assessment or inherited bias drift.

clauses.title: AI Risk Management Improvement
clauses.rationale: CA-07 continuous monitoring and AU-06 audit review provide systematic improvement feedback loops. PM-06 information security measures of performance and RA-07 risk response support structured improvement planning based on risk management effectiveness data.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.4.1 requires continuous improvement of AI risk management processes based on operational experience, new research findings, and evolving AI risk landscape. SP 800-53 improvement processes focus on security programme effectiveness and do not address AI-specific improvement drivers such as advancing AI safety research, new fairness methodologies, or updated responsible AI standards.

clauses.title: AI Incident Lessons Learned
clauses.rationale: IR-05 incident monitoring and IR-08 incident response plan updates provide structured lessons-learned processes. AU-06 audit review and AU-12 audit record generation support systematic review of incident data applicable to AI incident learning and process improvement.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.4.2 requires systematic incorporation of AI incident lessons learned into AI risk management processes, model development practices, and organisational AI policies. SP 800-53 lessons-learned processes focus on security incidents and do not address AI-specific incident analysis for bias events, model failures, or AI safety incidents.

clauses.title: AI System Decommissioning
clauses.rationale: CM-12 information location supports tracking AI system components for decommissioning. SA-12 supply chain protection and MP-06 media sanitisation cover data disposal aspects. PM-01 programme policies provide the policy framework for structured decommissioning processes.
clauses.gaps: AI RMF MANAGE.4.3 requires AI-specific decommissioning procedures covering model retirement, training data deletion, AI decision audit record preservation, and stakeholder notification of AI system discontinuation. SP 800-53 decommissioning controls address system and data disposal but not AI-specific decommissioning artefacts, model weight disposal, or AI audit record retention requirements.
